title: Ky Fan sums and inequalities
subtitle: G2 lecture 054000 · expanded companion
adaptation: Standalone slide treatment of the spoken lecture and display-only mathematical appendix; authored derivations, worked calculations and local SVG diagrams.

slides.title: From one singular value to a partial sum
slides.lead: The operator norm records only the strongest stretch. Ky Fan sums retain the strongest k stretches together.
body: Let A be a finite-dimensional linear map, and order its singular values σ₁ ≥ σ₂ ≥ ··· ≥ 0, with zeros appended when necessary. The kth Ky Fan sum adds the first k singular values. For k=1 it agrees with the operator norm; for k reaching the full list it becomes the nuclear norm.
Partial sums give a family of comparisons, one for each rank scale. That family will be the definition of weak majorization for singular-value lists.
slides.takeaway: A Ky Fan sum measures the total size of the k strongest singular directions.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 054000 · From one singular value to a partial sum

slides.title: The orthonormal-frame experiment
slides.lead: Choose k orthonormal input vectors and k orthonormal output vectors, and measure the total aligned action.
body: For k not exceeding either space dimension, vary input frame (vᵢ) and output frame (uᵢ) independently. Each pairing ⟨uᵢ,Avᵢ⟩ records how strongly the selected input direction lands on the selected output direction; take real parts in the complex case.
Align both frames with the first k singular-vector pairs. Every term then equals σᵢ, proving that the optimal pairing total is at least the Ky Fan sum.
slides.takeaway: Orthonormal frames supply a variational characterization of Kₖ.

slides.title: Why no other frames can do better
slides.lead: The singular-value decomposition turns every frame pairing into a weighted sum of singular values.
body: After expanding A in singular-vector pairs, Cauchy–Schwarz bounds each singular-direction coefficient by a product of two overlap lengths aⱼbⱼ. Bessel’s inequality gives 0 ≤ aⱼ,bⱼ ≤ 1 and square sums at most k.

Therefore the products wⱼ=aⱼbⱼ lie in [0,1] and have total at most k. For a decreasing nonnegative list, no such weights can exceed the sum of the first k entries. The singular frames attain equality.
slides.takeaway: Bessel and rearrangement bounds prove the frame characterization.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 054000 · Why no other frames can do better

slides.title: The Ky Fan triangle inequality
slides.lead: A fixed frame pairing is linear in the matrix, so it splits over A+B.
body: Take any admissible pair of frames. Its pairing total for A+B is the sum of its totals for A and for B. Each of those is bounded by the corresponding Ky Fan maximum.
Only after obtaining this bound for an arbitrary frame do we maximize for A+B. This proves the triangle inequality without trying to pair individual singular values entry by entry.
slides.takeaway: The variational formula gives the triangle inequality in one step.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 054000 · The Ky Fan triangle inequality

slides.title: Why an entrywise inequality fails
slides.lead: Two rank-one maps can combine into a full-rank map.
body: Take A=diag(3,0) and B=diag(0,3). The second singular value of each summand is zero, but A+B=3I has two singular values equal to three.
Thus σ₂(A+B) ≤ σ₂(A)+σ₂(B) is false: 3 ≤ 0 is impossible. The correct comparison sums the first k singular values, where K₁(A+B)=3 ≤ 6 and K₂(A+B)=6 ≤ 6.
slides.takeaway: Partial-sum domination survives even when entrywise singular-value comparisons fail.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 054000 · Why an entrywise inequality fails

slides.title: Pinching is an average of two unitary copies
slides.lead: Deleting off-diagonal blocks can be expressed as a two-term operator average.
body: For an orthogonal projection P, write J=2P−I. The reflection J is self-adjoint and unitary. Conjugating A by J changes the signs of the off-diagonal blocks but leaves both diagonal blocks fixed.
Taking the arithmetic mean of A and JAJ therefore removes the coupling. The Ky Fan triangle inequality and unitary invariance show that no Ky Fan sum increases.
slides.takeaway: The average-of-conjugates identity is the entire pinching proof.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 054000 · Pinching is an average of two unitary copies

slides.title: A small pinching calculation
slides.lead: The two-by-two matrix with rows (3,4) and (4,3) has singular values 7 and 1.
body: Pinching onto the coordinate axes leaves diag(3,3), whose singular values are 3 and 3. The first Ky Fan sum changes from 7 to 3, and the second from 8 to 6.

The pinched matrix has a larger second singular value than the original (3 versus 1), so this example also shows why the theorem must be stated using prefix sums rather than componentwise comparisons.
slides.takeaway: Pinching lowers every prefix sum without necessarily lowering every individual singular value.

slides.title: From Ky Fan inequalities to majorization
slides.lead: Compare x=(3,3) and y=(5,1), both in decreasing order.
body: Their first prefix sums satisfy 3 ≤ 5, and their totals are equal to 6. So x is majorized by y even though the second coordinate of x is larger.
This relation captures which singular-value lists are more evenly spread while preserving cumulative domination. The next step is to understand which norms respect all such inequalities.
slides.takeaway: Majorization compares sorted prefixes, not individual entries.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 054000 · From Ky Fan inequalities to majorization

slides.title: Three properties of the Ky Fan gauge
slides.lead: Ky Fan sums define unitarily invariant matrix norms for k within the singular-value list.
body: Their homogeneity follows because all singular values scale by the modulus of the scalar. Unitary invariance follows because U A V has the same singular values as A when U and V are unitary.
The triangle inequality comes from the frame maximum. Together these show how the elementary SVD creates a whole family of matrix norms.
slides.takeaway: The variational principle supplies all the norm axioms.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 054000 · Three properties of the Ky Fan gauge

slides.title: Reconstruct the main inequality
slides.lead: Begin with the SVD and rebuild the result without assuming a coordinatewise triangle inequality.
body: Use arbitrary orthonormal frames, expand their pairing sum through singular-vector pairs, and form the overlap weights. Show each weight is at most one and their sum at most k.
Then maximize for A+B, prove the prefix-sum triangle inequality, and apply it to the reflection average for pinching. Every step uses a precise property already established.
slides.takeaway: Frame variation, overlap weights, and reflection averaging form one connected proof.
